sundarikabhāradvāja.notes: MN 7 opens at Jeta’s Grove. At MN 7:19 the brahmin asks about bathing in the Bāhukā. DPPN puts the meeting on its banks. SN 7.9 and Snp 3.4 explicitly name Sundarika Bhāradvāja at the fire sacrifice on the Sundarikā. SN 7.8 concerns Aggika Bhāradvāja.

sundarikā.notes: MN 7 names the river in the bathing verses. SN 7.9 and Snp 3.4 place the sacrifice on its bank. The adjacent citations SN 7.8 and Snp 3.3 concern other episodes.

sundarī.notes: Thig 13.4 names the nun in the verses and the closing attribution. Her entry is missing. Sundarī 03 describes the female wanderer of Ud 4.8, also named in the chapter recap at Ud 4.10. Ud 4.8:4.3 has the wanderers themselves kill her and leave her in the ditch. The entry gives a different account. The word sundari at Snp 3.12:65.2 indexes the Sundarika Bhāradvāja discourse (Snp 3.4).

sundarīnandā.notes: Thig 5.4 addresses Nandā and credits the verses to Sundarīnandā Therī. DPPN’s reference to Thag verses 82–86 points to the wrong collection. Thag 1.82 is Kassapa’s. Among the AN references, AN 1.240 names Nandā foremost in meditation.

sunetta.notes: AN 7.66 recounts Sunetta’s cultivation of love. AN 6.54 and AN 7.73 also name him as the teacher who taught the way to the Brahmā world.

sunimmita.notes: AN 8.36 places Sunimmita among the Nimmānaratī gods. SN 40.11 and DN 11 name the godling. AN 8.37 and SN 40.10 are adjacent citation hits.

sunāga.notes: Thag 1.85 credits the verse to Sunāga Thera. His appearance at the end of Thag 1.90 is in the list of the chapter’s elders.

supassa.notes: The citation is unplaced. SN 15.20:4 names Supassa as the former name of Mount Vepulla when the people were called Suppiyā and Kassapa was the Buddha.

suppabuddha.notes: Ud 5.3 names the leper at Rājagaha. At Ud 5.3:11.5 the Pali says he spat, Sujato specifies the ground, and DPPN says he spat on Tagarasikhī. Suppabuddha 03 cites DN 14 for Vessabhū’s son, but DN 14:1.12 names Vessabhū’s parents and gives no son named Suppabuddha. The entry’s Buddhavaṁsa reference is outside the app’s books.

suppiya.notes: DN 1 calls Suppiya the wanderer traveling with his pupil Brahmadatta. Thag 1.32 credits Suppiya Thera, and Thag 1.40 lists him second in the chapter’s roster of elders. AN 1.264 and AN 8.91–117 name the laywoman Suppiyā. SN 15.20 names the Suppiyā people. Those three hits belong under suppiyā.

suppiyā.notes: The unplaced citation for the people corresponds to SN 15.20:4.2–5, which names them in Kassapa’s time. AN 1.264 singles out Suppiyā for nursing the sick. AN 8.91–117 explicitly calls her Suppiyā upāsikā. The neighboring AN 1 groups and AN 8.118–119 do not name her.

suriya.notes: The packet has no mentions. SN 2.10:1.2 calls him sūriyo devaputto, spelled with long ū and translated as the Sun God. DN 20:14.5–6 also has Sūriya leading his gods. DPPN reverses the actors after the release. In SN 2.10:6.1 Rāhu goes trembling to Vepacitti. SN 2.11 concerns Candimasa.

susīma.notes: SN 11.2 names the godling whom Sakka sends against the asuras. SN 11.1 sends Suvīra. SN 12.70 follows the Rājagaha wanderer through ordination and confession. Its Pali uses short-i Susima, a separate DPD headword, so the packet omits it. SN 2.29 also spells the god who praises Sāriputta Susima. DPPN treats his identity with Sakka’s general as conjectural. SN 12.69 is an adjacent citation hit.

sutanu.notes: SN 52.3:1.1 places Anuruddha at Sāvatthī on the bank of the Sutanu. The compound sutanutīre has its own DPD line, which explains the empty mention list. SN 52.2 gives only Sāvatthī.

sutanā.notes: AN 8.91–117 lists Sutanā among the laywomen. AN 8.89 and AN 8.90 concern monastic discipline.

suvīra.notes: SN 11.1 names Suvīra as the godling whom Sakka repeatedly summons. SN 11.10 mentions him only in the chapter recap.

suyāma.notes: All three packet passages call Suyāma a devaputta. Thag 1.74:1.5 credits the monk as Suyāmano thero, and Thag 1.80 repeats his name in the chapter roster. This is the alternate name given by Suyāma 04.

sādhuka.notes: SN 55.6:1.4 locates Isidatta and Purāṇa at Sādhuka. SN 55.5 is an adjacent citation hit.

sāgata.notes: AN 1.232 names Sāgata foremost in the fire element. The other two cited AN groups list nuns and laymen.

sāketa.notes: DN 16 lists the city and MN 24 names it in the relay of chariots. AN 4.24 places Kāḷaka’s monastery there and AN 5.144 places Tikaṇḍakī Wood there. Kakudha visits in SN 2.18, and the three elders stay there in SN 47.26 and SN 52.4. AN 4.23, AN 5.143, SN 2.17, SN 2.19 and SN 47.24–25 are neighboring citation hits. SN 44.1:1.3 gives Pasenadi’s journey from Sāketa to Sāvatthī. DPPN describes the reverse direction.

sālha.notes: AN 3.66 calls Nandaka’s visitor Migāranattā. The DPD example is numbered AN 3.67. AN 4.196 calls Sāḷha and Abhaya Licchavis. AN 3.70 and AN 4.200 have just the title Sāḷha in chapter recaps, with no epithet to distinguish the laymen there. Ānanda asks about the deceased monk of Ñātika in DN 16:2.6–7 and SN 55.8. The references landing on DN 17, SN 55.7, AN 3.65 and AN 4.195 miss their episodes.

sālā.notes: Both discourses named in the entry open in Sālā, the Kosalan brahmin village. The citation list places MN 41 alone and misses the Apaṇṇaka discourse at MN 60:1.2.

sāmagāma.notes: MN 104 opens at Sāmagāma, and DN 29:2.1 names the village where Cunda finds Ānanda. AN 6.21:1.1 uses sāmagāmake, a separate DPD headword, for the village with the lotus pond. MN 103 is set at Kusinārā.

sāmaṇḍaka.notes: SN 39.1–15 names the wanderer questioning Sāriputta at Ukkacelā. SN 38.16 belongs to the Jambukhādaka collection. AN 10.65–66 call the questioner at Nālaka Sāmaṇḍakāni, the entry’s variant and a separate DPD headword. SN 44.11 mentions Sāmaṇḍaka in a list of collections.

sāmāvatī.notes: The full DPPN entry identifies Udena’s queen with the laywoman foremost in loving-kindness at AN 1.261. Ud 7.10:1.3 names her at the head of the women who died in the royal compound. Its form sāmāvatīpamukhāni has its own DPD line. Of the cited AN 1 groups, only AN 1.258–267 names her.
